notes: Sitting MLAs for Punjab (16th Assembly, elected 2022), Haryana (15th Assembly, elected 2024), Himachal Pradesh (14th Assembly, elected 2022), Delhi (8th Assembly, elected 2025). Parsed from Wikipedia member-list tables (parse API) with rowspan-aware grid extraction; by-election / disqualification / resignation / defection updates applied through the most recent by-elections found (Punjab through 11 Nov 2025 Tarn Taran; HP through the Jun/Jul 2024 by-elections following the 6 Congress MLAs' disqualification and 3 independent resignations; no Haryana or Delhi assembly by-elections found as of 2026-09-25 — both houses are recent, elected Oct 2024 and Feb 2025 respectively). Party-wise stats computed from the deduplicated current-holder rows, not from the infobox 'Won' column (which reflects original election result, not current floor strength) or the infobox 'Bench' sub-table (which groups minor opposition parties together under a shared rowspan cell and does not cleanly split per-party). Two Punjab MLAs (Phillaur's Vikramjit Singh Chaudhary, Abohar's Sandeep Jakhar) were suspended from INC and are shown as IND per Wikipedia's current table, though press reports suggest they have since aligned with BJP informally — not confirmed via an official source, so left as IND with a note; flagged for a verifier pass. None of the four legislatures has a Legislative Council (all unicameral) so no st-<code>-legislative-council entities are included. pb: Punjab Legislative Assembly 117/117 seats, parties={'INC': 14, 'AAP': 95, 'BJP': 2, 'SAD': 1, 'IND': 3, 'BSP': 1, 'AD (WPD)': 1} | hr: Haryana Legislative Assembly 90/90 seats, parties={'BJP': 48, 'INC': 37, 'IND': 3, 'INLD': 2} | hp: Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly 68/68 seats, parties={'BJP': 28, 'INC': 40} | dl: Delhi Legislative Assembly 70/70 seats, parties={'BJP': 48, 'AAP': 22}
